summary: Malaysia's Immigration Department says the eVISA is only compulsory for 31 specific nationalities, for social visits. It says Chinese citizens on Ordinary or Public Affairs passports can enter visa-free for social visits of up to 30 days per entry from 1 September 2026, and that Indian nationals are exempt from the visa for social visits until 31 December 2026. Visitors must complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), which Canada's travel advice says is free and can be filled in up to three days before arrival.

driving.text: Malaysia is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). Malaysia's Road Transport Act 1987 (s. 28), published by the Road Transport Department (JPJ), says a driving licence issued in a country that is party to a treaty to which Malaysia is also party, and which recognises domestic licences issued by the contracting states, is deemed a Malaysian driving licence for as long as it remains in force in that country. The Act (s. 45G) sets the prescribed alcohol limit at 50 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood (22 micrograms in 100 millilitres of breath). The UK government says UK drivers need both the 1949 international driving permit (IDP) and their UK driving licence; Canada's travel advice says Canadian driver’s licences can be used in Malaysia for 3 months, after which you can either drive with an international driving permit or apply for a Malaysian driver’s licence at a certified driving institute. No official Malaysian source we could read states how long a visitor may drive on a foreign licence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Malaysia?
faq.answer: The United States is not on the Immigration Department's list of countries required to apply for a visa to enter Malaysia, and its eVISA FAQ says the eVISA is only compulsory for 31 specific nationalities; no official source we could read states how long US citizens may stay. Visitors must also complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online, which Canada's travel advice says is free and can be filled in up to three days before arrival.

faq.question: What is the MDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is the arrival form that the Immigration Department requires visitors to complete at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac. Canada's travel advice says it is a free online pre-arrival form that can be filled in up to three days before arrival.

faq.question: Can Chinese and Indian citizens visit Malaysia without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The Immigration Department says that from 1 September 2026 Chinese citizens on Ordinary or Public Affairs passports valid for at least 6 months can enter visa-free for social visits of up to 30 days per entry, and that Indian nationals are exempt from the visa for social visits until 31 December 2026. Visitors must also complete the MDAC.

faq.answer: No official page we could read states the eVISA fee. The MyVISA FAQ says the eVISA is only compulsory for 31 specific nationalities and that processing takes 2 to 7 working days.

levies.malaysia-tourism-tax.text: This Order comes into operation on 15 December 2025.

The rate of tourism tax to be charged and levied on a tourist staying at any accommodation premises is fixed at ten ringgit per night for each room and the imposition of the tourism tax shall be in accordance with section 6 of the Act.
Subject to subsection (3), it shall be the duty of the tourist to pay the tourism tax to the operator.
The following tourists are exempted from the payment of the whole of tourism tax: (a) a tourist who is a Malaysian national; and (b) a tourist who is a permanent resident of Malaysia.
